Fold the deprecated sampling arguments into sampleControl

Source: R/ctBackendSample.R
dot-ctSampleControlResolve.Rd

ctFit() took iter, chains and control as arguments of its own, which put three of a sampler's settings in the signature and the rest in a list – and made control mean rstan's control list on one backend and the julia sampler's settings on the other. They are all entries of sampleControl now.

Usage

.ctSampleControlResolve(
  sampleControl = list(),
  given = character(0),
  iter = 1000L,
  chains = 2L,
  control = list()
)

Arguments

sampleControl

The new list.

given

Names the caller actually used, from names(match.call()) in the calling function – a default cannot be told from a value that happens to equal it any other way.

iter, chains, control

The deprecated arguments, as they arrived.

Value

A list of iter, chains and control to carry on with.

Details

Resolved here rather than threaded through: everything downstream, on both backends, still receives iter, chains and control as it always did, so the rename cannot change what a fit does. In particular control still reaches stan unchanged on the stan path.

Precedence is sampleControl first, because it is the argument being kept. A deprecated argument that was *explicitly supplied* is used only for what sampleControl does not say, and is reported either way – a silent deprecation teaches nobody, and a silently ignored one is worse.
